item.text: The Corruption and Crime Commission examined theft and misuse risks involving dangerous pharmaceutical drugs in WA Health facilities.
item.support: The purpose of this report is to consider more broadly the issue of theft and misuse of dangerous and addictive pharmaceutical drugs

item.text: It analysed notifications about missing or otherwise unaccounted-for restricted drugs at three metropolitan hospitals from 2013 to 2017.
item.support: This report considers notifications received from WA Health relating to discrepancies in Schedule 8 and Schedule 4 Restricted drugs

item.text: The Commission concluded that most reported discrepancies remained unexplained after investigation.
item.support: Analysis of WA Health notifications (Table 6) suggests that most drug discrepancies remain unexplained after investigation.

item.text: It considered poor records and failures to follow security and handling policies to be contributing factors.
item.support: the difficulties experienced by WA Health in explaining drug discrepancies is exacerbated by deficiencies in record keeping and compliance with policies

item.text: Its nine recommendations covered consistent policies, accountability, records, security, prompt reporting, skilled investigations, staff training and detection strategies.
item.support: Ongoing education and training be given to relevant staff in drug management, record keeping, reporting discrepancies and investigating discrepancies.

item.quote: WA Health is unable to account to the Commission or the community for the majority of drug discrepancies.
